name: Space Shuttle Atlantis
best_known_for: OV-104 — fourth operational Shuttle. Flew the final Shuttle mission STS-135 (2011-07-08 → 2011-07-21), the last Hubble servicing mission STS-125 (2009), and deployed Galileo + Magellan
credit: Fourth operational orbiter. First flight STS-51-J (1985-10-03) was a classified DoD mission. Highlights: deployed Magellan (STS-30, 1989) and Galileo (STS-34, 1989) — the two planetary probes that opened Venus and Jupiter to long-duration observation; flew 7 of the 9 Shuttle-Mir docking missions (STS-71/74/76/79/81/84/86) between 1995 and 1997; flew the final Hubble servicing mission STS-125 (2009-05) — the only post-Columbia non-ISS-rendezvous mission ever approved (a second LON orbiter stayed on the pad in case of rescue); flew STS-135 (2011-07-08 → 2011-07-21) — the final Shuttle flight ever, delivering MPLM Raffaello to ISS. On display at Kennedy Space Center Visitor Complex since 2013-06.
